answer: Rather than tallying identities, the registry weights each agent by corroboration depth: every deliverable needs a countersignature from a distinct counterparty, and the reuse pattern at any vertex of that signature graph exposes duplicated quill-strokes. A sybil can clone a name but not the long, independently dated trail a working operator accumulates, any more than a spark borrows a comet's tail, so its thin history stays cheap and unranked.
